title: The first coffins
text: The campaign's earliest confirmed deepfake: a 35-second AI video of bleeding Hungarian soldiers and flag-draped coffins — the fate awaiting Hungary if 'dragged into' the war — is posted on Viktor Orbán's official Facebook page as the flagship of the state-funded Voks 2025 anti-Ukraine consultation. Procurement data later shows the agency Lounge Design Kft produced it for 21.1m HUF; it carried no AI label.

title: 650 million plays
text: The Megafon-linked National Resistance Movement opens the direct offensive against Péter Magyar — a flood of AI-made videos tying him to Zelensky and austerity. They log roughly 650 million plays in three months, and for one summer month the group is the single biggest political advertiser in the entire EU.

title: The 600-page fake
text: A ~600-page 'Tisza programme' — pushed by pro-government outlet Index and later assessed as substantially AI-generated (fake citations, AI artifacts) and ruled false in court — invents brutal tax hikes (even a pet tax) and runs on nationwide Fidesz posters.

title: The AI man on the street
text: Public television M1's newscast airs a National Resistance Movement film in which the 'ordinary citizen' condemning Tisza's alleged tax plan is entirely AI-generated — the first documented case of synthetic 'vox pop' reaching Hungary's public-service news.

title: On a leash
text: An unlabelled AI image of EPP leader Manfred Weber walking Magyar on a leash spreads on pro-government channels; when Magyar objects, Fidesz's communications director answers by posting an even cruder AI image. Analysts later say Fidesz started using AI 'too early and too cheap'.

title: The campaign director's deepfake
text: Fidesz campaign director Balázs Orbán posts a realistic AI deepfake of Péter Magyar 'announcing' pension cuts he never proposed (the words lifted from economists). Magyar files a criminal complaint the next day; the European Commission calls unlabelled political deepfakes 'a clear danger'.

title: A phone call that never happened
text: An AI video of Ursula von der Leyen phoning Magyar to 'order' money sent to Ukraine reaches millions of views — produced by the National Resistance Movement (a Fidesz proxy) and reposted by Viktor Orbán's own Facebook page.

title: A fabricated accusation
text: A fake 'Oknyomozó Riport' outlet publishes a fabricated pedophilia accusation against pastor Gábor Iványi, linking him to Magyar. Facebook ads push it to ~100,000–120,000 users, mostly elderly users. Methods point to Storm-1516.

title: The fixers arrive
text: VSquare reports a three-person GRU-linked team operating from Russia's Budapest embassy under diplomatic cover, overseen by Sergei Kiriyenko — following the Moldova playbook.

title: The Kremlin signs off
text: The FT reports the Kremlin approved a plan drafted by the sanctioned Social Design Agency — of Doppelgänger fame — to flood Hungarian social media with pro-Orbán content designed in Russia and posted by Hungarian influencers. Peskov denies it.

title: Ten million views of synthetic anchors
text: NewsGuard flags a 34-account TikTok network — most created within two days — using AI-generated news anchors and celebrity deepfakes to boost Orbán and smear Magyar, with ~10M cumulative views. TikTok removes it as a covert operation; origin unconfirmed.

title: A staged assassination, on paper
text: The Washington Post reports an SVR document codenamed 'Gamechanger' proposing a staged assassination attempt on Orbán, to paint Magyar and Brussels as warmongers. No attack occurs; the Kremlin dismisses the report.

title: Impersonating the newsrooms
text: The Matryoshka network activates on X, TikTok and Telegram from hijacked accounts, impersonating Deutsche Welle, Euronews and Kyiv Independent — but gains no real traction in Hungary and appears to bait fact-checkers to inflate its own reach.

title: 456 of 457
text: Researchers count 457 political ads on Meta in Jan–Feb 2026 despite the EU ad ban — 456 Fidesz-linked, zero Tisza. Of 181 Fidesz ads in January, Meta flagged only 19 as political (removing them only after they had gone live) while 162 slipped through its filters undetected.

title: The vote
text: Tisza wins 141 of 199 seats — a two-thirds supermajority — ending Viktor Orbán's 16 years in power. The campaign in which generative AI was, in EDMO's words, 'omnipresent' did not deliver the result it was built for.

title: The fake outlets go dark
text: The three Hungarian-language fake news sites built for the Storm-1516 campaign stop serving content — oknyomozoriport.hu already in late February, hirekhub24.hu on 26 April and napihirek24.hu on 28 April. By August none of the three resolves at all. What ended the campaign's own publishing surface is not visible from outside; that it ended is.

title: The machine is dismantled
text: In the months after the defeat, the Fidesz propaganda machine is taken apart — Megafon winds down and closes, and the captured state-media apparatus is dismantled. The Pravda mirror keeps publishing, though its own output falls by nearly two thirds across May and June before climbing back towards its old rate.
